sources.news_title: Man accused of shooting woman to death in Baton Rouge arrested during traffic stop in Downtown Memphis, police say
sources.text:
MEMPHIS, Tenn. - A man accused of shooting a woman to death in Baton Rouge was arrested during a traffic stop in Downtown Memphis, police said.
Memphis police officers stopped the car at South Second Street and Pontotoc Avenue just before 7:45 p.m. Thursday.
Police said officers found the woman dead in the passenger seat. MPD later determined she was not killed in Memphis.
The Baton Rouge Police Department (BRPD) identified the woman as 50-year-old Lanessa Bradford.
According to BRPD, Bradford was with 50-year-old Tyronne Brazille at a Baton Rouge park when the two got into an argument. Police said Brazille shot Bradford.
BRPD said Brazille drove through several states before Memphis police stopped him.
Brazille was taken into custody in Memphis. He is awaiting extradition to Baton Rouge, where he will face a murder charge.

sources.news_title: Man arrested after police allegedly find dead woman in car during traffic stop
sources.text:
Man arrested after police allegedly find dead woman in car during traffic stop
MEMPHIS, Tenn. (WMC/CNN Newsource/WKRC) — Police arrested a man after they reportedly found a deceased woman in his car during a traffic stop.
According to reporting from WMC, 50-year-old Tyronne Bazille was stopped in Memphis Thursday night, and officers found 50-year-old Lanessa Bradford dead from a gunshot wound in the passenger seat.
Detectives say Bazille and Bradford were together at a public park in Baton Rouge, Louisiana, when they had a disagreement and Bazille shot Bradford before fleeing the area. He drove through several states before being stopped for a traffic violation.
Bazille was arrested and is awaiting extradition to Baton Rouge, where he is facing a murder charge.

Man arrested after allegedly shooting woman, driving 5-plus hours with body in passenger seat
MEMPHIS, Tenn. (WAFB/Gray News) - A man has been arrested after he allegedly shot a woman in Louisiana and drove with the victim dead in the passenger seat to Tennessee.
According to the Baton Rouge Police Department, Tyronne Brazille, 50, was taken into custody after being pulled over for a traffic violation in Memphis.
Police said that during the traffic stop, they discovered the victim, Lanessa Bradford, 50, dead in the vehicle. Officers said Bradford was found with a gunshot wound.
Louisiana authorities said the shooting occurred at Independence Community Park in Baton Rouge, adding they believe Bradford was shot after getting into an argument with Brazille.
Brazille was taken into custody as a fugitive in Tennessee and is awaiting extradition to Baton Rouge. His charges include murder in connection with Bradford’s death.

sources.news_title: Man who allegedly killed woman in Baton Rouge caught in Memphis with body in passenger seat
sources.text:
A man has been arrested after he allegedly shot a woman in Baton Rouge and fled with her body to Memphis, Tennessee.
The Memphis Police Department contacted Baton Rouge police to report they had stopped 50-year-old Tyronne Brazille for a traffic violation on Thursday and discovered Lanessa Bradford, 50, dead in the passenger seat from a gunshot wound, according to a BRPD news release.
Baton Rouge police say the shooting happened at Independence Community Park, 7500 Independence Blvd., after Brazille and Bradford allegedly got into a verbal argument.
Brazille then fled the area and drove through several states before being stopped in Memphis, the release states.
He was taken into custody in Memphis as a fugitive and is awaiting extradition to Baton Rouge. He will face a charge of murder in connection with Bradford’s death, police said.

Baton Rouge man arrested in Memphis after woman found dead in car during traffic stop
BATON ROUGE — A Baton Rouge murder suspect was arrested in Memphis, Tennessee, after a woman's dead body was discovered in the passenger seat of a vehicle, according to the Baton Rouge Police Department.
According to the department, on Thursday, officers with the Memphis Police Department discovered 50-year-old Lanessa Bradford dead in the passenger seat while conducting a traffic stop on a vehicle. Officers said that Bradford had suffered from a gunshot wound.
Detectives later learned that Bradford and the driver of the vehicle, 50-year-old Tyronne Brazille, were previously together at Independence Community Park on Independence Boulevard in Baton Rouge.
According to the Baton Rouge Police Department, Brazille allegedly shot Bradford following a verbal disagreement and fled the area, driving through several states before being stopped in Memphis for a traffic violation.

sources.news_title: Police Say Louisiana Man Drove Across States With Woman’s Body
sources.text:
Man Accused Of Shooting Woman in Louisiana, Driving To Tennessee With Body In Passenger Seat
BATON ROUGE, La. — A Baton Rouge man is awaiting extradition to Louisiana after police say a traffic stop hundreds of miles away uncovered the body of a woman who had been shot.
Tyronne Brazille, 50, was taken into custody in Memphis, Tennessee, on Thursday, August 13, after officers pulled him over for a traffic violation, according to the Baton Rouge Police Department.
What officers reportedly discovered inside the vehicle quickly turned the traffic stop into a homicide investigation.
Police said 50-year-old Lanessa Bradford was dead in the passenger seat of Brazille’s vehicle. Authorities said she had suffered a gunshot wound.
Police Say Shooting Happened At Baton Rouge Park
Investigators traced Bradford’s death back to Independence Community Park in Baton Rouge.
According to BRPD, investigators believe Brazille and Bradford were together at the park when the two became involved in a verbal argument. Police allege Brazille then shot Bradford.
Authorities say Brazille left Baton Rouge after the shooting with Bradford’s body still inside the vehicle. Another local report indicates he traveled through multiple states before eventually being stopped by Memphis police.
Baton Rouge and Memphis are separated by hundreds of miles, making what began as an alleged shooting at a Louisiana park an investigation stretching across state lines.
Traffic Violation Ends Alleged Trip Across Multiple States
Police have not publicly detailed what traffic violation prompted Memphis officers to stop Brazille.
That stop, however, ultimately led officers to Bradford and Brazille’s arrest.
Brazille was taken into custody in Tennessee as a fugitive, according to Baton Rouge police. He is now awaiting extradition back to Louisiana.
Murder Charge Expected In Baton Rouge
BRPD says Brazille will face a murder charge in connection with Bradford’s death once he is returned to Baton Rouge.
Authorities have not released additional information about the relationship between Brazille and Bradford or further details about what allegedly led to the argument at Independence Community Park.
